final.label: type-and-initialization-choice

skill_entry.name: Declaration types and initializers: unsigned for counts, initialized struct locals, const literal globals, no redundant initializer sweeps
skill_entry.trigger: Production files (h/, src/), any one: (a) SIGNED COUNT: an added or re-added local, parameter, out-parameter or member of type int, int32_t, int64_t or long whose name carries a count word (count, cnt, blocks, bytes, size, _per, total, idx, index, num_, len), while the same quantity is unsigned at the reviewed commit: a producer, a sibling helper's parameter, the field it is stored to (in that field's header), or a `(uint64_t)(name` cast. (b) UNINITIALIZED STRUCT LOCAL: an added local of struct type with no initializer, the struct declared in the diff or in a header the diff touches, with no user-provided constructor. (c) MUTABLE LITERAL GLOBAL: an added UPPER_CASE namespace-scope variable initialized from a literal, with no const or constexpr. (d) INITIALIZER SWEEP: the PR body says it adds default member initializers across a struct.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. (a) Grep the diff for signed count declarations. Take names from the hits and line numbers from a full-file grep at the review commit (REV). Collect every type REV gives each name, the field the value is assigned to and that field's header type, and every `(uint64_t)(name` cast. A `< 0` or `= -1` use clears the name. Names declared together form one group; one unsigned anchor makes the whole group a finding. 2. (b) Print the struct at REV; count members with an initializer. Some missing: note a read after a loop that is the only writer. 3. (c) Grep writes, excluding the definition line; none: finding. 4. (d) Find the `new T` spelling and whether T has a user-provided constructor; state the rule from the standard. 5. Answer guideline questions with 'no written rule'. 6. Rerun 1 and 2 at every push.
skill_entry.question: Can this value ever legitimately be negative or change after startup, and does the code that produces, stores or consumes it already use the unsigned (or const, or initialized) form at the commit under review?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A pre-existing signed declaration left in place where the hunk only adds an initializer (PR 2193 5e2d19d362:h/pos/device.hpp:215,221). Scalar locals and scalar members without initializers (PR 2011 src/pos/driver.cpp:850-852, h/pos/dma/queue.hpp:45-46). A global initialized from a function call (src/pos/mwaitx.cpp:27). Mixed unsigned widths (17c6e0117d:src/pos/worker.cpp:1095-1100). A struct whose members all carry initializers at REV (Wade withdrew, 2790148917). A local whose struct lives in an untouched header or has a user-provided constructor (PR 3008 h/pos/regs.hpp locals; tron-3756 process_device_id). A class member of struct type. Constant spelling (check 13). Post the pattern once per group, not per line (PR 2011: two of four locals commented). Never block; approve while open.
skill_entry.finding_shape:
(a) Round 1, one prose comment on the declaration group: '`<name>` and `<siblings>` (<file>:<line>) are `int`; <anchor> at :<line> is `uint64_t`. never expected to be negative, right? wouldn't `uint64_t` make more sense? same for `<sibling>`?' Later push: one ```suggestion block per signed signature line that remains. (b) '```suggestion
  <T> <x> = {};
```
? (`<T>` at <header>:<line> has no default member initializers at <commit>; initializers in the struct are the alternative)'. (c) '```suggestion
const <type> <NAME> = <expr>;
```
that is... if we don't plan to ever change this value?'. (d) 'a bit pedantic: <T> has <no user-provided constructor, so `new T()` already zero-initializes | a user-provided constructor, so <members> are the only ones this covers>; being explicit is fine. Approved.'
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit or minor; his own words are 'these 3 variables below are never expected to be negative right?' (3430026641), 'a bit pedantic' (4125818552), a bare '?' after a suggestion block (2789725609), and 'that is... if we don't plan to ever change this value?' (2380221355). He approves while these stay open (PR 3008 approved 2026-06-18 after the three suggestion blocks were applied; PR 2438 approved in the same review that called it pedantic). 'kinda pedantic' (2789826297) is a different nit in PR 2011 about default parameter values and belongs to missing-explanation-at-declaration.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file at the commit the review is on (REV: producer and consumer signatures, struct definition, writes to the global); callers in the same file; the header that declares the field the value is stored to (h/pos/device.hpp) and the struct definition (h/pos/device.hpp, h/pos/dma/queue.hpp); PR body for pattern (d) (the stated reason and 'values already set by constructor or init()'); no CI, no runtime.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check: declaration types and initializers

Placeholders: WT (worktree), N (PR number), HEAD (final head), REV (the commit the review is on; HEAD when reviewing the final head), BASE (see 0), FILE, HEADER, NAME, T.

0. BASE. For an open PR `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main`. For a merged PR take the merge commit M (`gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N -q .merge_commit_sha`) and use `git -C WT merge-base REV M^1`. Confirm `git -C WT merge-base --is-ancestor BASE REV` exits 0 before any step. (`merge-base REV origin/main` returns REV itself once the PR is merged.)

1. Signed count declarations added by the diff:
   `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE REV -- src h | grep -E '^\+[^+].*\b(int|int32_t|int64_t|long)[ &]+([a-z_]*(count|cnt|blocks|bytes|size|total|idx|index)[a-z_]*|[a-z_]*_per(_[a-z_]*)?|num_[a-z_]*|len|[a-z_]*_len|len_[a-z_]*|[a-z_]*_len_[a-z_]*)\b'`
   Take only the NAMES from the hits. Take REV line numbers from the step-2 full-file grep; do not compute lines from `@@` headers (a 499-line hunk gave numbers 2 lines off).
   A hit counts as added when its declaration sits inside a function the PR creates or rewrites (the enclosing function has `+` or `-` lines in the -U0 diff, or the declaration is removed in one hunk and re-added in another: PR 3008 locals at BASE :1187-1192 reappear at REV :1693-1696 and Wade commented). A declaration left in place where only an initializer is added is the do-not-fire case (PR 2193 `int num_devices = 0`).
2. For each NAME, every type the file gives it:
   `git -C WT show REV:FILE | grep -n -E '\b(int|int32_t|int64_t|long|uint32_t|uint64_t|size_t)[& ]+NAME\b'`
   Cast anchors: `git -C WT show REV:FILE | grep -n -E '\(uint64_t\)\(NAME\b'` (every hit; PR 3008 has four).
   Field anchor: `git -C WT show REV:FILE | grep -n -E '\.[a-z_]+ = NAME;'`; take the field F from the hit, then `git -C WT grep -n -E '\b(uint32_t|uint64_t|size_t) F;' REV -- h`. A `return NAME;` in another function is not an anchor.
   Negative use (clears the row): `git -C WT show REV:FILE | grep -n -E 'NAME *(<|<=) *0|NAME *= *-1'`.
   Grouping: names declared in one out-parameter list or one consecutive block form a group. One unsigned anchor for any member makes the group the finding; name the anchored member first and the rest as siblings. The fix width is the anchor's width at round 1 (uint64_t from h/pos/device.hpp:139 on PR 3008) and the width the author already chose at a later round.
3. Uninitialized struct-typed locals added by the diff:
   `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE REV -- src h | grep -E '^\+\s+(struct )?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_:<>]*\s+[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*;\s*(//.*)?$' | grep -v -E '^\+\s*(return|co_return|throw|delete|goto|break|continue|using|typedef)\b' | grep -v -E '^\+\s+(std::|boost::)' | grep -v -E '\b(int|uint[0-9]+_t|int[0-9]+_t|size_t|bool|float|double)\s'`
   For each type T find its header: `git -C WT grep -l -E 'struct T\b|class T\b' REV -- h src`. Keep the line only when that header is in `git -C WT diff --name-only BASE REV` or T is declared in the diff, the line is a local (not inside a class body), T has no user-provided constructor (`grep -n -E '\bT\(' HEADER` inside the struct body is empty), and the local does not exist verbatim at BASE. Otherwise drop it (PR 3008: nine h/pos/regs.hpp register-field locals, header untouched, Wade silent).
   Struct at REV: `git -C WT show REV:HEADER | sed -n '/struct T {/,/^};/p' | grep -n -E '^\s+[A-Za-z_].*;'`; count members with an initializer (`=` or `{...}`) and without.
   Zero-iteration read: `git -C WT show REV:FILE | sed -n 'L1,L2p'` around the local; note whether the only writer is inside a `for`/`if` and a read follows it.
4. Mutable literal globals added by the diff:
   `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE REV -- src h | grep -E '^\+[A-Za-z0-9_:<>]+\s+[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+\s*=' | grep -v -E 'const|constexpr|\w+\([^)]*\);$'`
   Writes, definition line excluded first:
   `git -C WT grep -n -E '\bNAME\b' REV -- src h | grep -v -E '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:\s*[A-Za-z0-9_:<>]+\s+NAME\s*=' | grep -E 'NAME\s*(=[^=]|\+\+|--|\+=|-=)|&NAME\b'`
   A remaining assignment, increment, address-of or non-const reference argument is a write. Empty: finding. (PR 1485 at 08b5f10085: empty; uses :60 and :83 are `"a"(MWAIT_C0)` asm input operands.)
5. Initializer sweep (pattern d):
   `gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json title,body -q '.title + "\n" + .body' | grep -n -i -E '(add|default|explicit|consisten|safe)[^.]{0,80}initializ|initializ[^.]{0,80}(add|default|explicit|consisten|safe)'`
   A sentence that removes initializers (tron-2774 'removing runtime field initialization') does not trigger. Pattern (d) also needs an added count above zero:
   `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE REV -- HEADER | grep -c -E '^\+.*(= 0;|= false;|= nullptr;|= \{\};|= -1;)'`
   Creation spelling: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'new T\b' REV -- src h`; record `()`, `(args)` or nothing per hit. Constructor: `git -C WT show REV:HEADER | sed -n '/^  T(/,/{/p'`; a `T(...)` with a body or initializer list is user-provided.
   Rule to state: `new T()` value-initializes a class with no user-provided constructor, so every member is zero before default member initializers apply, with or without any such initializer. `new T` without parentheses default-initializes, so members without a default member initializer stay indeterminate. A class WITH a user-provided constructor runs it under either spelling; members neither in its initializer list nor given a default initializer stay indeterminate. Grade each added initializer redundant-but-harmless or needed; approve either way.
6. Guideline check: `git -C WT ls-tree --name-only REV AGENTS.md t/AGENTS.md .github/AGENTS.md ingest/AGENTS.md` first (git grep ignores a missing pathspec silently; at 40e4cea98609 only AGENTS.md and ingest/AGENTS.md exist), then `git -C WT grep -n -i -E 'initializ|unsigned' REV -- <files that exist>` (empty at 2026-10-06) and `grep -n -i -E 'unsigned|initializ' ~/.claude/skills/cpp-coding-guide/SKILL.md` (only the literal-0 line). Say 'no written rule'.
7. At every later push rerun steps 1 and 3 against the new REV: the author applies the ask to the locals and misses the helper signatures (PR 3008), or moves the fix into the struct (PR 2011); withdraw or narrow the finding accordingly.

On PR 3008 (merge commit 17c6e0117d; BASE dd5dd82caf for the review commits 40e4cea98609 and c68ea87f48, BASE 8811bdd35f for the final head): at 40e4cea98609 step 1 lists 22 src/pos/worker.cpp lines: block_layout members :1083-1086, compute_block_layout :1096-1098, `int pad_per` :1103, new helper out-parameters :1118-1121 and :1240-1242, fill_rxinfo :1480, write_rx_descriptors :1506-1507, locals :1693-1696 (`int expected_blocks = 0; int res_per_block = 0; int res_bytes_per_block = 0; int64_t pad_bytes = 0;`, re-added from BASE :1187-1192). Step 2 adds the pre-existing producers :565-568 and :750-752 (`int&`, `int64_t&`, present at BASE as :558-561 and :743-745), the field anchor :1492 `rx_entry.results_per_block = res_per_block;` -> h/pos/device.hpp:139 `uint64_t results_per_block;`, the casts :1519, :1524, :1532, :1555; no negative use; the group of four locals is the round-1 finding (3430026641). At c68ea87f48 step 1 lists exactly :1481 `int res_per_block,` :1507 `int res_bytes_per_block,` :1508 `int64_t pad_bytes) {` (3437522787, 3437526764, 3437527579). At 17c6e0117d step 1 is empty. Step 3 at 40e4cea98609 lists nine h/pos/regs.hpp locals, all dropped (header untouched, present at BASE). On PR 2011 (BASE ab75e61d83, REV e091f3f799): step 3 lists h/pos/hwattention.hpp :502, :578, :627, :657 `dma_xfer_state`; the keyword filter removes seven `return` lines; the struct at e091f3f799:h/pos/device.hpp:187-196 has 0 of 5 members initialized (finding, :627 read at :646 after the `for` at :635); at d4795f37a5 (commit c2d72e6a7f) 5 of 5 (withdraw). On PR 1485 (08b5f10085): step 4 lists src/pos/mwaitx.cpp:16 `uint32_t MWAIT_C0 = (0xF << 4);`, write grep empty (finding), :27 `bool MWAITX_SUPPORTED = is_supported();` filtered. On PR 2438 (fc4fc8780a, merge-base 9ebe06083e): step 5 counts 50 added initializers in h/pos/device.hpp, `new PosDevice(index++, ...` at src/pos/device.cpp:72, user-provided constructor at h/pos/device.hpp:340-356 (idx, enqueued_work, dequeued_work, pci_*, iommu_group, vfio_fd(-1), regions(), allocator_), so the explicit initializers are the only guarantee for the members the constructor and init() do not set. Silent corpus (15 diffs): step 1 lists tron-1707 src/pos/fake.cpp:160 `int idx` and tron-4353 h/tron/models/model.hpp:2877 `int64_t total`, both cleared by step 2; steps 3, 4, 5 list nothing after the filters.
final.widen_delta: n/a: disposition add_new; no existing check reads declaration types or initializers. Closest neighbour is check 13 (constant names): it owns the stem and suffix of a constant, this check owns its const-ness and the signedness and initialization of counts and struct locals. residual_risks: Negative space for pattern (a) was scanned only over the 15 silent diffs in corpus/silent-diffs, not all 48 silent PRs; two grep hits remain there (tron-1707 `int idx`, tron-4353 `int64_t total`), both cleared by step 2, so a future silent PR with an unsigned sibling of a signed count would fire where Wade might stay silent.

Grouping rule: at 40e4cea98609 only res_per_block (field anchor) and res_bytes_per_block (casts) have unsigned anchors; expected_blocks and pad_bytes join the finding only through the consecutive-declaration grouping, which has one corpus precedent (3430026641).

Step 1 also lists 18 other signed declarations on PR 3008 round 1 (block_layout members, helper parameters) that Wade did not comment on; the author widened them himself at c68ea87f48 and 17c6e0117d. The round-1 shape posts one prose comment on the local group, so the extra lines produce no extra comments, but an agent must not post suggestion blocks on them at round 1.

Pattern (b) finding-shape offers `= {}`; for a type with a user-provided constructor `= {}` may not compile, so the trigger excludes that case, but a struct with a deleted default constructor and no user-provided one is not handled.
Width when siblings disagree (uint32_t vs uint64_t) has no corpus precedent; the procedure takes the anchor's width.
The step-4 definition-line exclusion assumes the global is defined on one line with the type immediately before NAME; a definition split across lines would count as a write and suppress the finding.
